title: Stability liaison action grid & risk heatmap — SLO rollout playbook
content:
Purpose and quick summary:
This doc is a working playbook for the cross-functional SLO program focused on: 1) a lightweight liaison role per product/capability, 2) an action-grid to guide decisions during rollout, and 3) a compact risk heatmap that teams can use during pre-launch and post-launch retros.

Why this exists (short):
- We keep seeing SLOs defined in isolation and then hitting gaps at launch (monitoring, runbook alignment, ownership of fallback policies).
- Goal: reduce launch delta (defined = shipped) by clarifying actions and decision thresholds per liaison.

Audience: SREs, product owners, platform engineers, monitoring owners, release managers.

Top-level objectives:
- Make each product/capability have a named "stability liaison" accountable for SLO readiness before canary (not just on-call).
- Provide a simple decision grid so rollouts are uniformly gated (observability, rollback, fallback).
- Provide a risk heatmap with clear remediation steps and runbook references.

Roles and responsibilities (proposed):
- Stability Liaison (one per product/capability): coordinates SLO readiness checklist, chairs pre-canary review, maintains liaison log. (Suggested: 20% sprint allocation during rollout weeks.)
- Product Lead: defines customer-impact assumptions, acceptable regressions, and escalation path.
- SRE Owner: verifies telemetry (metrics/logs/traces), runbooks, and on-call play alignment.
- Observability Owner: ensures dashboards and alerts exist per SLO and that dashboards show both total and per-route signals.
- Release Manager: enforces gating and records decision decisions in the action-grid.

Stability Liaison quick template (copy into user doc):
- Name / team / Slack / Pager duty: 
- Capability covered (service, endpoint, route):
- Nominal SLO(s): e.g., availability 99.95% (30d) for control-plane, latency p95 < 250ms for short-generation endpoints
- Critical metrics to verify: request success rate, p50/p95 latency, error budget burn rate, cold-start rate, KV cache hit ratio
- Runbook links: 
- Obs dashboards (URL):
- Pre-canary checklist status: [observability, runbooks, fallback, canary traffic routing, A/B gating]

Action Grid (decision matrix) — use during gating meetings. Columns = Condition; Rows = Action. Keep it simple:
- Condition A: Missing critical telemetry (no per-route latency). Action: Halt canary, create ticket to add metric, assign to Observability owner. Temporary mitigation: route 0% traffic to new binary.
- Condition B: Alert firing at non-critical threshold but low burn (error-budget burn rate < 3x). Action: Continue canary, enable tighter logging, schedule debugging session next day.
- Condition C: Error budget burn rate >= 3x AND user-impact > minor. Action: Roll back to previous stable variant, start incident review, tag the SLO as "blocking" in release notes.
- Condition D: Small regressions (latency p95 increase < 10% absolute and no user-facing failures). Action: Continue canary with expanded telemetry for 24–48h. Consider canary hold.

Decision thresholds (proposal):
- Block launch if: missing >1 of [per-route latency, per-route success rate, alerting rule, runbook].
- Rollback trigger: sustained error-budget burn rate > 5x for 1 hour OR user-visible error rate > 0.5% on core paths for 15 minutes.
- Hold trigger: burn rate 2–5x OR p95 increase > 25% vs baseline.

Risk heatmap (3x3) mapping and remediation notes: 
- Axis: Likelihood (low/med/high) x Impact (low/med/high) — color-coded in dash but here as categories.
- Examples: 
  - High likelihood, high impact: New multi-tenant caching layer (risk: cache stampedes -> widespread latency regressions). Remediation: rate-limited rollout, pre-warm cache, canary with traffic shaping and auto-fallback to stateless path.
  - High likelihood, medium impact: New metrics pipeline consumer causing delayed metrics for 5–10m. Remediation: add synthetic monitors and fallback metrics queue; set alert for staleness.
  - Low likelihood, high impact: Release that changes auth header parsing for 3rd-party integrators. Remediation: integration test gate + partner opt-in canary; communicate to partners.

Operational checklist (pre-canary, canary, full rollout):
- Pre-canary (must pass all): obs dashboards exist per route; canary routing automation ready; liaison checklist completed; rollback docs exist with steps and target variant; synthetic tests pass in staging.
- Canary (must monitor continuously): watch p50/p95, error budget burn rate, real-user anomalies; liaision to post hourly updates to the action-grid; 0.5–1% traffic initial ramp, then exponential step-up.
- Full rollout (post gates): ensure runbook is published to internal runbooks repo; schedule 7-day post-launch pulse to examine SLI drift and to adjust SLO thresholds if needed.

Suggested SLO templates (examples — teams should adjust):
- Control plane API (short RPCs): Availability SLO = 99.99% (30d) measured as successful 2xx responses, exclude planned maintenance windows, exclude rate-limited 429s if client-side. Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms (normal workload).
- Long generation endpoint: Availability SLO = 99.9% (30d). Latency SLOs are percentile-banded with user-impact tiers: p50 < 1s, p95 < 4s (non-embeddings), allow p99 to be higher but tracked.
- Embeddings batch pipeline: Throughput SLO = maintain >= 90% of expected batch throughput while average queue time < 500ms.

Observability minimal list (must-have signals):
- Success rate (per route)
- Request latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) per route
- Error budget remaining and burn rate (windowed)
- Synthetic heartbeat (end-to-end)
- Resource pressure signals (GPU queue depth, mem/cpu, disk io where relevant)
- Request route breakdown (to isolate traffic shifts)

Communication cadence and templates:
- Pre-canary sync: 30-minute meeting with PM, liaison, SRE owner, release manager. Use the action-grid to record result.
- Hourly canary updates (chat + brief note in grid): liaison posts short status: green/amber/red + key metric deltas. Link sample template.
- Post-mortem / pulse: 1 week after full rollout, 60–90 minute review to capture SLI drift, lessons, remediation backlog.

Quick templates (copy/paste):
- Hourly update format: [time] status: GREEN/AMBER/RED; p95: +Xms; errors: Y%; actions: created JIRA-#### assigned to @owner
- Pre-canary pass note: Pre-canary checklist: OBS ✅ RUNBOOK ✅ FALLBACK ✅ LOADTEST ✅; canary window requested: 2h starting 09:00 PDT

Open questions / unresolved items (for program leads):
- Should liaison be a rotational role (3 months) or permanent (longer)? tradeoffs: knowledge vs context switching.
- Standardize burn-rate thresholds across services with widely different traffic profiles — do we normalize by traffic volume or by user-impact buckets?
- How to automate loa- and burn-rate detection into an auto-hold gate without too many false positives?

Next steps (actionable):
- Pilot with 3 product teams this quarter: search-service, hosted-api (short gen), and embeddings-pipeline. Assign liaisons and checklist owners. (Owner: Jordan Kim)
- Create a small adjacency repo: /ops/slo-playbook/templates with the liaison template and action-grid matrix (PR: #212 referenced above). (Owner: Marcus Lee)
- Add automatic burn-rate alerting recipe to observability repo and test it in staging. (Owner: Aisha Patel)

Notes to self / draft artifacts:
- Keep this doc intentionally compact — it should be a one-page read for an oncall or PM prepping a canary. Longer playbooks live in Confluence + runbooks.
- We'll iterate on thresholds after pilot; capture team-specific calibrations in the liaison log.

Appendix: sample short SLO entry (text to paste into SLO catalog):
- service: hosted-api-abacus
- endpoint: /v1/generate (short)
- sli: successful_responses / total_requests (exclude 429) - window: 30d
- slo_target: 99.90%
- alerting: page when error_budget_remaining < 15% and burn_rate > 3x for 30m

End of draft.

-- Jordan K. (draft, updated 2026-08-24)
